transcript: okay so I am gonna talk about Audra McDonald's performance as Mama Rose but I'm gonna go a little bit in depth on this because I have complicated feelings and I also have complicated feelings about those complicated feelings like the “short version” of this isn't how I feel the long version is how I feel so if you don't feel prepared to hold some nuance and hop on this train of thought with me then please honestly just skip this video so a lot of people have said that Audra McDonald is miscast as Mama Rose some people said that when it was announced some people have said that after seeing the performance part of the reason being that Rose is traditionally a belting role and Audra McDonald is famously not a belter and before I saw the show I heard those arguments and I said “okay, I'm pretty sure that's not gonna bother me” why? several reasons first of all, in general acting is a lot more important to me than singing even in musical theatre and maybe even *especially* in musical theatre where frankly really skilled acting can be kind of hard to find oops who said that? I'm also really not a fan of how so much of musical theatre has become this contest to see who can belt the highest, the loudest, and the longest And this mentality of like “if you don't sing in that one acceptable style and if it doesn't sound exactly like how I remember it on the cast recording it's automatically bad” This attitude has flattened and deteriorated the sense of character in the musical theatre canon and it bugs the hell out of me so like I have defended my fair share of controversial vocal performances in my day and lest we forget this is Audra McDonald we're talking about here the G.O.A.T who has more skill in her left ear than most Broadway stars have in their entire body and the final reason that I felt confident that it wouldn't bother me is that rose is onstage for a huge portion of this fairly long show she only has so many of those big high singing moments so dismissing the other 2h45m of her performance just because of those few moments is ridiculous and yet after all of that it did bother me and I have had to spend this entire week trying to reconcile that involuntary reaction with what I believe in principle and in that reflection process there are a couple things that I have come to reluctantly accept first of all on that last point I made these moments might be a small portion of the show quantitatively but they stick in your brain and for better or for worse it's hard not to think of those moments when formulating your impression of how the role was sung that's partly because the songs have become iconic but also because they were written to stick in your brain in the first place because they are narratively significant which brings me to the second thing that I have begrudgingly come to accept which is that while I can criticize the culture of putting belting on a pedestal in this case the songs were in fact written for that voice type not just in terms of what they thought would sound good but also in terms of how they were telling the story quick disclaimer that I did train as a singer for like 8 years but it has been a while so I might botch some of the terminology here but I think hopefully you'll get what I'm trying to say for me I think the problem wasn't the lack of belting it's that the notes fell kind of on her passagio kind of low in her head voice range and I think that's what prevented it from having that imposing, cathartic release effect that the writers intended to convey when they wrote it like I can't help but wonder if it would have worked better if they had raised the keys or adjusted the melody or even if she like jumped the octave I don't know if that would work But like in general adjusted the music upward not because higher = better but because it would sit at a place in her range that more closely corresponded with the place in the actor’s range that it was originally written to sit I often think of musical theatre as the actor using music as a tool for expression but I'm reminded that the composer is likewise using the actor as a tool for expression to execute the storytelling that is written into the music and that's where Audra MacDonald brilliant as she is G.O.A.TED as she is was maybe the slightest bit miscast but also I wanna say like like screw that!!! because she still sang the hell out of it and she still acted the hell out of it and her take on rose is so freaking good in all other respects like I might get comments on this video agreeing with me and I'm gonna get mad at those people and be like “hey, that's Audra McDonald you're talking about watch your mouth!!” so yeah like this was my honest opinion but also don't agree with me!!!
